items.prompt: What does an extension's items.xml primarily define?
choices: Types and attributes for the extension's type system.
items.answer: Types and attributes for the extension's type system.
items.explanation: SAP documents items.xml as the place to define new types and extend or override attributes, subject to the schema and release behavior.

items.prompt: Choose a model for a product's current sustainability rating and an independently queryable audit history.
items.answer: A source-backed rating attribute or composed item for the current value plus a separate source-backed audit item and relation for history; document cardinality and ownership.
items.explanation: The requirement combines current read efficiency with historical identity and queryability; a single serialized blob would make audit queries and lifecycle harder.

items.prompt: A type created in Backoffice disappears after initialization. What is the likely explanation?
items.answer: It was a runtime type without a source-backed items.xml declaration; initialization rebuilds the type system from extension declarations, so the runtime type is not recreated.
items.explanation: SAP documents this distinction and the absence of generated Java sources for runtime-only types.

items.prompt: Why can an out-of-order itemtype definition fail a build even when each individual type is valid?
items.answer: The items.xml schema/parser processes definitions in order and inheritance dependencies must be available before subtypes are defined.
items.explanation: The SAP items.xml reference documents single-pass ordering and build failure for invalid order.
